ctor.rationale: `base(-1, CardType.Skill, CardRarity.Rare, TargetType.Self)` with `protected override bool HasEnergyCostX => true` (Cascade.cs:10-15) == `energy_cost_x = True` (cards/base.py:84-87) plus `_energy_cost = 0`. The -1 sentinel does NOT carry the unplayable-cost finding here: `CardEnergyCost`'s constructor sets `Canonical = ((!CostsX) ? canonicalCost : 0)` (CardEnergyCost.cs:86), so an X-cost card's base is 0 in C# too -- the sim's 0 is exactly right, and `GetWithModifiers`'s `if (CostsX) return num` short-circuit matches `Card.energy_cost`'s X handling at the play site.

OnPlay.rationale: `int num = ResolveEnergyXValue(); if (IsUpgraded) num++;` (Cascade.cs:19-23) == `num = self.captured_x + (1 if self.upgrade_level > 0 else 0)`; `captured_x` is set by the play pipeline as `hooks.modify_x_value(card, player.energy)` (combat.py:547-549), which is the sim's ResolveEnergyXValue (the Chemical-X style hook). The sim then reimplements `CardPileCmd.AutoPlayFromDrawPile(num, CardPilePosition.Top, forceExhaust: false)` (Cascade.cs:24) inline and does so faithfully: it pulls all `num` cards off the TOP of the draw pile FIRST, reshuffling the discard in when the pile runs dry, and only then auto-plays them in order -- matching CardPileCmd.cs:937-965's two-phase pull-then-play with its per-iteration ShuffleIfNecessary (CardPileCmd.cs:941) and its `FirstOrDefault()` top-of-pile pick (945; the sim's `draw_pile.pop()` is the same end, since the sim stores its draw pile top-LAST). `forceExhaust: false` needs no counterpart.

OnUpgrade.maps_to: handled inline as `+ (1 if self.upgrade_level > 0 else 0)` (cascade.py:34)
OnUpgrade.rationale: Cascade.cs declares NO OnUpgrade override -- the upgrade changes no printed number, it adds 1 to the count read from `IsUpgraded` inside OnPlay. The sim mirrors that exactly, including having no `_on_upgrade`.

guards.what: Cascade must not auto-play itself when its own effect triggers a reshuffle (Cascade.cs holds the card in PileType.Play; the sim parks it in the discard pile)
guards.rationale: The sim removes itself from `discard_pile` for the duration and restores it in a `finally` (cascade.py:38-40, 59-61), on top of the `_playing_card` limbo marker the reshuffle already honours (combat.py:452-454). Belt-and-braces, and the outcome matches C#'s Play-pile exclusion.

guards.what: the pull loop stops when both piles are empty, and again when an AfterShuffle listener drains the pile (cascade.py:46-53)
guards.rationale: C# `AutoPlayFromDrawPile` breaks on `cardModel == null` after ShuffleIfNecessary (CardPileCmd.cs:949-952), which is the same two conditions. The sim's comment names the Stratagem case explicitly.

guards.what: the play loop bails on `ctx.combat.is_over or ctx.player.is_dead` (cascade.py:56-57)
guards.rationale: C# breaks the play loop on `item.Owner.Creature.IsDead` (CardPileCmd.cs:958-964) and `CardCmd.AutoPlay` additionally early-returns on `CombatManager.Instance.IsOverOrEnding` (CardCmd.cs:53-56). Both sides stop; the cards already pulled stay out of the draw pile either way.

guards.what: during the PULL phase C# has already moved each card into PileType.Play (CardPileCmd.cs:954); the sim holds them in a local list, in no pile at all (cascade.py:44-54)
guards.rationale: Same observable outcome, so this is a re-architecture rather than a gap: the cards are out of the draw pile on both sides and land in their normal result piles after playing. The only difference is which pile a hook listener would see them in DURING the pull, and the sim has no card-in-Play-pile listener category at all (the hook_dispatch seam records the missing Play-pile position as its own finding). Recorded so the difference is visible rather than silent.
